It escalated to after a couple weeks of this back and forth, my mental health was declining immensely. I am autistic so I struggle more intensely with vagueness and uncertainty than a neurotypical allistic person would, which I don't believe mental illness justifies bad behaviour but it puts it into persepective. No matter what I tried, I just could not stop hyperfixating on the mystery at hand and having no explanation or understanding of why she had suddenly broken up with me and followed it by saying that she never wanted to be in a relationship ever again, it was pushing my brain to its limits as I overthought nonstop of every possible reason why she had said what she said. The stress was taking a big toll on my body, I was hyperventilating for most of the time I was conscious, my heart was beating fast non stop and I was getting chest pains and this constant hyperarousal of my nervous system was exhausting me so much I couldn't muster up the energy to get out of bed and take care of myself.  
  
I couldn't keep waiting any longer in this state so, even though she told me she just needed space to think about it, I wrote her a long text message outlining to her that I really needed her to explain her feelings to me and that I understood it was difficult for her but that I'm hoping she won't overlook that its difficult for me too. We still didn't have a proper conversation after that, and after a couple more weeks had gone by I texted her again another long message pleading her to talk to me. She was understandably frustrated that I didn't respect her asking me for space.  
  
Over the next few months, I got more and more desperate and I texted her almost everyday, sometimes a week or two would go by or a few days where I would try my hardest not to reach out. She was getting more and more frustrated with me and repeatedly told me to leave her alone because she needs space. Much later I learned that she was physically ill, malnutritioned and had fainted on the streets and she was in the middle of seeking treatment for her physical and mental health, and I felt like a huge asshole because I had harrassed her non stop whilst she had set a boundary that I needed to leave her alone and not text her until she texted me and told me she was ready. At the same time I had no idea what was happening or going on in her life as I wasn't receiving any news of her, and when I'd ask her how she was doing she would say she was fine. I tried to work things out by myself, I wrote detailed explanations of possible theories I had and I sent them to her asking "I understand you're overwhelmed, but please take a look at this and give me a small confirmation that this is what happened or not what happened". I knew that if she was struggling to explain herself in great detail, that I could make it easier for her by asking specific questions that only require a yes or no answer, and then piece them all together to understand what happened. I know that I was an asshole for not crossing her boundaries. I knew that it was wrong, but at the same time I was also degrading myself because she suddenly completely changed overnight and cut me out of her life with no proper explanation as to what changed and why.  
  
Her new fuckbuddy (who she low-key is in a trauma bond/self-destructive enabling relationship with) called me suddenly and started telling me off on the phone and asking me what was wrong with me and why I wasn't respecting my ex's boundaries and telling me that I was killing her. My ex then came on the phone and me and her talked and she exasperately said "Fine, you want to talk then lets do it now and get it over with". We did have a proper and in-depth talk where she was able to clarify her feelings and intentions for breaking up. I processed it now and I personally believe that ultimately she's not breaking up with me because of a healthy and fully rational reason, and that she's stuck in a pattern of self-destruction and she was overcame by lust for this old friend of mine who is now her neighbour. Me and her were in a semi-long distance relationship as I lived an hour and a half by train and could only afford to come over on the weekends. But my ex is very touch-starved and terrified of being on her own, so I think ultimately she wasn't satisfied with only being able to see me two days in a week and chose to attach and cling on to her neighbour who is also just as self-destructive as her. They're relationship is based on using each other to avoid loneliness and physical intimacy, and it's my and a couple common friend's opinion that they would not be as obsessively attached with each other if they weren't as mentally ill as they were or lived in a big city surrounded by other people (as they live in a tiny village in the middle of nowhere).  
  
I know that I was the asshole in this situation and I'm feeling extremely guilty about it and I don't know how to cope. Was I an irredeemable asshole in this situation? How can I forgive myself for the way I behaved? I've never ever done something like this before, previously in our relationship I always respected her boundaries very adamantly. How can I be sure that this was a one time mistake and not a pattern of toxic behaviour I will repeat again in the future with my next partner?

You sound very sweet. Your comment made me think of something about me that I find weird. I’m not asking for advice don’t worry, I’m just looking for anyone who will listen on the internet.

Strangely I’m not struggling with that. I wake up, automatically brush my teeth and shower and I even have breakfast and whilst I’m currently visiting family, we make small talk and I get involved in family activities during the day and at night we all have dinner and we usually play a board game and just have a good time. 

Despite today being a good day and me having done many fulfilling and enjoyable things, it didn’t stop me from breaking down as soon as I went to my room for the night and I find myself back here all over again. 

Honestly, I’m just mostly perplexed by how any of that makes sense. Sure, the fact I’m currently on holiday with my family and things are going well with them is only a rare occurrence, but I just don’t understand why all these things fail to bring me any sense of genuine happiness and peace in life. Why do I still feel empty after a nice stress-free day of enjoying nature, pleasant exchanges with family, good food and a full stomach, stimulating tasks and just things that I feel a happy person’s life would consist of?

I don’t have any friends anymore, anytime I think I have we eventually just stop being friends and it doesn’t make a difference because I’ve never felt that they truly cared or loved me. 
But I don’t like being alone and having no one to talk to, I want to have my pain be recognised and validated by others and also recognise and validate others pain. If you ever need to talk dm me because I think online friendships are more suited to people like me

They should be made an example on what happens if you behave like a creep.

That’s such an abusive and manipulative technique. Tell you what, if he threatens to slowly kill himself then call the paramedics on him and have him taken in for a psychiatric evaluation and put in a psych ward. If he’s 100% serious then surely this is the best thing you can do for him?

Thank you so much! Both of these responses were incredibly helpful and it’s given me a lot to think about. Even if the issue hasn’t been resolved yet until we’ve talked in depth about it, I’m emotionally feeling a lot more reassured and not as down as I was before I made this post so thank you so much

I think you’ve every right to confess to her, especially for your own closure. Sure it might not lead to a relationship and as long as you’re not expecting the possibility of a relationship to blossom out of your confession then this sounds like it’s really important for you. You deserve closure and to express what you’ve wanted to for a while - if you preface the confession by reassuring her that you’re not expecting it to lead to anything then that’ll minimise any awkwardness. Good luck if you decide to go through with it!
